test_title: PYST 05: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 06 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the Gram Sabha in the context of the Panchayati Raj system in India?

options.text: An advisory council of State representatives
The deliberative assembly of all eligible village residents
A judicial body for urban areas

solution:
The correct answer is __**The deliberative assembly of all eligible village residents**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gram Sabha** refers to the assembly of all eligible voters in a village-level administrative unit within the Panchayati Raj system in India.
 
• It serves as a primary democratic institution, where decisions regarding village development, welfare activities, and local governance are deliberated upon.
 
• The Gram Sabha is responsible for approving the annual budget and development plans prepared by the Gram Panchayat.
 
• It ensures transparency and accountability in the functioning of the Gram Panchayat by allowing villagers to question and scrutinize its activities.
 
• As per Article 243A of the Indian Constitution, every Gram Sabha is a statutory body functioning at the village level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchayati Raj System:**

 
 
• It is a decentralized form of governance in India, introduced through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992.
 
• It consists of three tiers: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zilla Parishad (district level).
 
• The system aims to empower rural areas and ensure participatory democracy.
 
 
 
• **Article 243:**
 
 
• Articles 243 to 243-O in the Indian Constitution deal with the Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• These articles provide the framework for the composition, powers, and functions of Panchayati Raj bodies.
 
 
 
• **Role of Gram Sabha:**
 
 
• It acts as a watchdog over the Gram Panchayat, ensuring transparency and accountability.
 
• The Gram Sabha can approve or reject plans, schemes, and budgets proposed by the Gram Panchayat.
 
• It provides a platform for villagers to voice their concerns and actively participate in governance.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Gram Sabha:**
 
 
• Promotes direct democracy at the grassroots level.
 
• Encourages participation from marginalized and underprivileged sections of society.
 
• Acts as a medium for collective decision-making on local issues.
